response.justification: The candidate brings genuine geospatial domain experience (founder of GISCollective, Green Map work, FOSS4G speaker) and proven low-latency systems work in DLang at Sociomantic, plus strong Linux and testing discipline. However, the role requires modern C++ or Rust as the primary language, and his C/C++ exposure is dated (2014–2015 at National Instruments), with recent years focused on TypeScript/Node full-stack product work. He also lacks direct routing/navigation pipeline experience, making him a plausible but risky fit worth a technical screen rather than a clear yes.
strengths: Deep geospatial/GIS domain experience via GISCollective and Green Map projects
Low-latency, high-throughput systems experience (async I/O, caching, fibers) at Sociomantic
Strong engineering craftsmanship: TDD, CI/CD, Linux, and open-source contributions
concerns: Modern C++/Rust experience is minimal and outdated; primary systems language is DLang
No direct experience with routing engines, tiling, or navigation guidance systems
Recent roles are TypeScript/Node full-stack product work, drifting from systems engineering
